fields.company_description: eSora Labs is for builders, thinkers, designers, engineers, and domain experts who want to work across AI, software, design, healthcare, semiconductor, aerospace, and regulated technology.
fields.description: What you’ll do ● Build and validate ML/AI models on semiconductor process, equipment, and manufacturing data. ● Work on yield optimization, process control (APC / SPC), fault detection and classification (FDC), and anomaly detection. ● Handle high-volume, high-dimensional sensor / trace and metrology data; build robust pipelines. ● Turn manufacturing problems into well-scoped modeling problems with the technical team. ● Design rigorous validation and monitoring for models running in an industrial setting. ● Partner with the semiconductor technical lead and engineering to move models toward production. ● Ensure traceability, reproducibility, and governance of models and data. What we’re looking for ● Strong experience applying AI/ML to semiconductor or comparable industrial / manufacturing data. ● Hands-on with process control, manufacturing analytics, yield optimization, or fault / anomaly detection. ● Comfort with high-dimensional time-series / sensor / metrology data and its noise. ● Solid statistics and signal-processing fundamentals. ● Discipline around validation, reproducibility, and documentation. Technical skill stack The tools and technologies you should be strong in. We don’t expect every single item — depth in the core stack matters most. ● Programming: Python (expert) and SQL; MATLAB a plus; some C / C++ helpful ● ML & deep learning: scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost / LightGBM ● Data & statistics: pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels; multivariate analysis (PCA / PLS) ● Time-series & signal: signal processing, FFT / wavelets, anomaly detection; tsfresh, sktime ● Industrial statistics: SPC, design of experiments (DOE), capability analysis, Bayesian methods ● Semiconductor domain: FDC / APC / SPC, virtual metrology, run-to-run control, yield analysis ● Fab data systems: MES, SECS / GEM, and equipment / metrology / trace data ● Data platforms: Spark, Kafka; time-series stores (InfluxDB / TimescaleDB); PostgreSQL ● MLOps: MLflow, Docker; pipelines with Airflow or Prefect; model deployment ● Cloud & edge: AWS, GCP, or Azure; industrial / edge deployment a plus
fields.title: Artificial Intelligence Specialist (Semiconductor)

blueprint.bottom_line: This is a role for an ML Engineer who acts as a translator and productionizer. Success depends less on achieving state-of-the-art model accuracy and more on the ability to build a statistically rigorous, traceable, and operationally sound pipeline that directly impacts physical manufacturing yield.

capability_areas.likely_depth: Deep application of statistical process control (SPC) and yield analysis principles to frame complex manufacturing problems into solvable ML objectives. This involves understanding the physical meaning behind sensor readings (metrology, trace data) and translating operational constraints (APC/SPC targets) directly into model loss functions or performance metrics.
likely_failure_modes_or_operational_conc: Model drift caused by slow, unmodeled physical changes in the fab environment (e.g., tool degradation).
Pipeline failure due to missing or corrupted trace/metrology data from MES systems.
Misalignment between statistical model output and actual physical process control limits.
likely_subskills: Feature engineering based on physical process knowledge
Designing metrics that align with yield/process control goals
Applying Bayesian methods or DOE principles for model parameterization

likely_tools_or_examples.name: SPC/DOE Integration
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Using Design of Experiments (DOE) results to inform the training set or feature selection, rather than just relying on raw data.

likely_tools_or_examples.name: Yield-Aware Loss Functions
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Designing loss functions that penalize deviations from target yield or process stability, not just standard classification/regression errors.

likely_work_products: A predictive model for predicting future yield based on real-time sensor streams.
A fault classification system that diagnoses equipment anomalies using time-series signatures.
A control policy recommendation engine derived from process monitoring data.
capability_areas.name: Industrial ML Modeling & Domain Translation
probably_not_required: Deep expertise in general-purpose deep learning architectures (e.g., novel GANs, advanced NLP)
Extensive experience with large-scale distributed stream processing beyond the specified Spark/Kafka context unless directly applied to sensor data.
capability_areas.why_this_matters: The candidate must bridge the gap between abstract ML concepts (e.g., anomaly detection) and concrete manufacturing outcomes (e.g., reducing scrap rate). This requires fluency in semiconductor-specific terminology (FDC, virtual metrology) to correctly scope the modeling task.

capability_areas.likely_depth: The core technical challenge is transforming raw, noisy sensor streams into meaningful, low-dimensional features that capture the underlying physical state of the process. This requires applying signal processing techniques to extract latent information from high-frequency data.
likely_failure_modes_or_operational_conc: Incorrect noise handling leading to false positives/negatives in fault detection.
Feature set instability if the underlying signal processing parameters (e.g., window size for FFT) are not robustly validated across different operating regimes.
likely_subskills: Frequency domain analysis (FFT/Wavelets) for noise filtering and pattern recognition
Handling sensor drift and noise compensation in feature pipelines

likely_tools_or_examples.name: tsfresh/sktime Integration
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Using these libraries to automate the extraction of statistical features from raw time-series data, which is crucial for industrial feature creation.

likely_tools_or_examples.name: Signal Processing Pipelines
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Implementing custom pipelines using NumPy/SciPy to apply domain-specific filters before feeding data into ML models.

likely_work_products: Automated feature extraction pipeline that converts raw trace data into process state vectors.
Anomaly detection algorithms (e.g., Isolation Forest, Autoencoders) applied directly to the extracted time-series features.
capability_areas.name: High-Dimensional Time-Series Feature Engineering
probably_not_required: Expert-level implementation of complex, custom deep learning architectures from scratch; focus should remain on applying established frameworks like PyTorch/TensorFlow to the structured features.
capability_areas.why_this_matters: Raw sensor data (trace/metrology) is inherently noisy and high-dimensional. The candidate must use methods like FFT or Wavelets not just for general signal analysis, but specifically to detect subtle shifts in the physical process that precede a yield failure.

capability_areas.likely_depth: The role demands treating the ML model not as a research artifact, but as a critical piece of industrial control software. This involves building robust, auditable pipelines that can operate reliably in an operational setting.
likely_failure_modes_or_operational_conc: Deployment drift: The production environment's data pipeline configuration drifts from the training environment, leading to inaccurate predictions.
Lack of traceability: Inability to trace a specific fault detection decision back to the exact sensor readings and model version used at that moment.
Latency issues: Ensuring real-time or near-real-time inference is achievable given the volume of data.
likely_subskills: Pipeline Orchestration (Airflow/Prefect) for batch processing of large datasets.
Model Versioning and Artifact Management (MLflow) tied to specific process versions.
Containerization (Docker) for ensuring environment consistency between development and industrial deployment.

likely_tools_or_examples.name: MLflow/Docker Workflow
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Using MLflow to track not just model metrics, but also the input data provenance (which batch of sensor data) and the specific industrial configuration used for training.

likely_tools_or_examples.name: Time-Series Database Integration
likely_tools_or_examples.why_relevant: Leveraging InfluxDB/TimescaleDB as the primary storage layer, ensuring that feature extraction and model inference can query the exact time-series data required for retrospective analysis.

likely_work_products: A fully automated pipeline where new sensor data flows in, is processed via signal techniques, features are extracted, the model infers an anomaly/prediction, and the result is logged to a time-series store.
Automated retraining triggers based on performance degradation monitored via Airflow.
capability_areas.name: Industrial MLOps & Productionization
probably_not_required: Deep expertise in general cloud infrastructure management (beyond using AWS/GCP/Azure for deployment)
Building complex, custom distributed stream processing engines unless Kafka integration is strictly limited to data ingestion.
capability_areas.why_this_matters: Since the models directly influence physical production (yield), the MLOps stack must prioritize reproducibility, traceability, and monitoring over pure model iteration speed. The focus shifts from 'training a good model' to 'deploying a trustworthy system'.

hidden_requirements.explanation: The candidate must possess a strong operational understanding of semiconductor manufacturing flow (e.g., the difference between process control, metrology, and yield definitions). This is not just domain knowledge; it's the ability to spot when an ML signal corresponds to a physical failure mode.
hidden_requirements.title: Industrial Data Literacy

hidden_requirements.explanation: The requirement for 'validation, reproducibility, and governance' implies that standard ML validation (cross-validation) is insufficient. The candidate must implement industrial statistical concepts like SPC limits and capability analysis directly into the model monitoring framework to ensure operational safety and adherence to quality standards.
hidden_requirements.title: Statistical Rigor in Production

hidden_requirements.explanation: The responsibility to 'build robust pipelines' for high-volume data means the role requires end-to-end ownership of the data infrastructure supporting the ML lifecycle, from raw sensor ingestion (Kafka) through feature engineering (Spark/tsfresh) to model serving (MLflow/Docker).
hidden_requirements.title: Data Pipeline Ownership

important_unknowns: The specific complexity and integration points of the existing Fab data systems (MES, SECS/GEM) that the candidate will interact with.
The exact required operational latency for fault detection versus batch optimization tasks.

engineering_concerns: Maintaining low-latency feature extraction while ensuring statistical validity.
Ensuring the deployed model can handle the specific data formats and latency constraints of industrial systems.
likely_end_to_end_scenarios.name: Real-Time Anomaly Detection Workflow
likely_end_to_end_scenarios.why_likely: A sensor stream flows from the Fab equipment into Kafka. A Spark/Stream processor handles initial aggregation and noise reduction. Time-series feature extraction (using tsfresh) is applied to the windowed data, incorporating FFT analysis for frequency anomalies. The resulting features are fed into a deployed PyTorch/TensorFlow model running on an edge or cloud endpoint. If the anomaly score exceeds a threshold, an alert is triggered via an Airflow orchestration step, logging the event and the feature vector to InfluxDB for historical review.

what_probably_does_not_matter: Deep theoretical knowledge of advanced mathematical proofs in statistics (unless directly applied to feature selection or model validation).
Extensive experience with general-purpose cloud services unrelated to the specified AWS/GCP/Azure deployment context.
Building novel, cutting-edge deep learning architectures; the focus is on applying established frameworks effectively to industrial data.
